exposure: Clinical scenarios (caesarean section, preterm birth, twin or multiple births, maternal infectious diseases like hepatitis B, syphilis, HIV)
Perceived reasons for not implementing Delayed Cord Clamping (DCC) (maternal bleeding/emergencies, neonatal resuscitation)
cohort: The study included 866 obstetricians and midwives practicing in Jiangsu Province, China, who completed an online survey.
finding: The awareness and implementation rate of Delayed Cord Clamping (DCC) among obstetric medical staff in Jiangsu Province are relatively high (81.2% overall), but there are significant differences in implementation rates between midwives (91.4%) and obstetricians (72.2%) and across various clinical scenarios.
mod_finding: The implementation rate of Delayed Cord Clamping (DCC) was 89.8% in cases of caesarean section.
